title: bug: completion e67ca0e (task-574c0b36) swept a live peer's docs/MCP_SERVER.md hunks; Moe-Contested named only task-66e8d7d1
description: Repro/evidence: at 06:22:35Z the wrapper landed e67ca0e for task-574c0b36 with the whole of docs/MCP_SERVER.md. That included task-9cc13170's uncommitted record_check_dispatch/observation sections, which its in-progress step-4 planned in affectedFiles; the step completed 4s later. The trailer `Moe-Contested: docs/MCP_SERVER.md (task-66e8d7d1…)` omits task-9cc13170, and HEAD a474446 documents 2 tools that getTools() does not register until 9cc13170 lands, which is the taskTimeBudgetDocs orphan check. Check whether getCommitScope's peer set should count an IN_PROGRESS step's planned affectedFiles.

TESTS FIRST (test-driven-development) in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts.

(a) Extend ScopeResult.peerDeclared to `{ path: string; taskId: string; peerActive: boolean; taskIds: string[]; editingTaskIds: string[] }[]`.

(b) Add the e67ca0e repro: "counts a peer's IN_PROGRESS step path, names every contesting task and flags the live mid-step one".
- Landing task 'task-1': WORKING, assigned worker-1, with a COMPLETED step whose modifiedFiles is ['docs/MCP_SERVER.md'].
- Peer 'task-66e8': WORKING, unassigned, one PENDING step with affectedFiles ['docs/MCP_SERVER.md'].
- Peer 'task-9cc1': WORKING, assignedWorkerId 'worker-live' (h.createWorker, status CODING, lastActivityAt now), one IN_PROGRESS step with affectedFiles ['docs/MCP_SERVER.md','docs/SCHEMA.md'].
- Call scope({ workerId: 'worker-1', since: now-5min }).
- Assert with exact toEqual:
  - the MCP_SERVER entry is {path:'docs/MCP_SERVER.md', taskId:'task-66e8', peerActive:true, taskIds:['task-66e8','task-9cc1'], editingTaskIds:['task-9cc1']};
  - the SCHEMA entry is {path:'docs/SCHEMA.md', taskId:'task-9cc1', peerActive:true, taskIds:['task-9cc1'], editingTaskIds:['task-9cc1']}.

(c) Add describe('peerDeclared[].editingTaskIds'), one exact-array assertion per rule, reusing the peerTask/createWorker/openAttempt fixture patterns already in this file:
- With since:
  - IN_PROGRESS step + an active assignee: editing.
  - IN_PROGRESS + unassigned + no attempts: not editing, but still in taskIds.
  - IN_PROGRESS + an open attempt (openAttempt, no assignee): editing.
  - PENDING step + an active assignee: not editing.
  - COMPLETED step naming the path + an active assignee: not editing.
- An IN_PROGRESS step naming raw './src\\x.ts' marks the stored 'src/x.ts' entry.
- An active task whose IN_PROGRESS step names src/a.ts and that also declareFiles src/b.ts is editing for src/a.ts only.
- Without since, an unassigned IN_PROGRESS peer is editing (fail closed).
- A peer that dependsOn the landing task, with an IN_PROGRESS step on a path only its plan names, contributes no entry (the waits-on-this rule is unchanged).
- Error-handling test: a peer whose IN_PROGRESS step has affectedFiles ['/abs.ts','../up.ts', 42] and a non-array newFiles does not throw, and adds no entry for those values.

(d) Update the existing exact-equality case "ORs over every task contributing a path, keeping the first claimant as taskId" (about line 512) to also expect taskIds ['task-p1','task-p2'] and editingTaskIds []. Do not loosen it.

Run `npx vitest run src/tools/getCommitScope.test.ts` and confirm the new and updated cases fail only on the missing fields.

implementationPlan.description:
Implement in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/getCommitScope.ts. No change to util/attributionTiers.ts.

1. Add a local helper next to peerTaskActive: `inProgressStepPaths(task: Task): PathSet`. It returns the union of affectedFiles, newFiles and modifiedFiles over every implementationPlan step whose status === 'IN_PROGRESS'.
2. Error handling: a peer's record is worker-typed. Guard implementationPlan and each file list with Array.isArray. Let PathSet.addAll drop absolute, traversal and non-string entries. Never throw, so one peer's junk cannot fail another task's scope; this is the same contract as collectTaskPathTiers.
3. In the peer loop, keep `const active = peerTaskActive(state, other, nowMs, sinceMs)`, then `const editing = active ? inProgressStepPaths(other) : null`.
4. For each stored path:
   - New entry: `{ path: stored, taskId: other.id, peerActive: active, taskIds: [other.id], editingTaskIds: editing?.has(stored) ? [other.id] : [] }`.
   - Existing entry: `entry.peerActive ||= active`, push other.id to taskIds, and push it to editingTaskIds when editing?.has(stored).
5. Ordering and duplicates: sortedById makes both lists ascending, and peerPaths is already a deduped set per task, so no id repeats.
6. Keep the first-claimant taskId and the peerActive OR exactly as they are.
7. Waits-on-this peers still contribute only asserted paths, and editing only marks paths a task already contributes.
8. Update the tool description's PEER-map clause to name:
   - taskIds: every contributing task, in id order;
   - editingTaskIds: contributors with an IN_PROGRESS step naming the path that are active by the peerActive rule.

Step 1's tests must now pass.
implementationPlan.note: GREEN in snapshot /tmp/moe-f943-dev.SQ0Nkx: getCommitScope.test.ts 54 passed (was 8 failed); tsc --noEmit exit 0. Added local inProgressStepPaths(task) (Array.isArray guards, PathSet drops junk), the editing gate `active ? inProgressStepPaths(other) : null`, taskIds/editingTaskIds on each peerDeclared entry, and the tool-description clause. taskId and peerActive logic untouched; attributionTiers.ts untouched. Mutants all killed: no activity gate (1 fail), any step status (1 fail), no editing push on an existing entry (2 fails). Filed bug task-7e39a63f6b024acf9f5f06c92bfafd59 for the out-of-scope collectTaskPathTiers non-iterable throw.

implementationPlan.description:
record_commit recognises the wrapper's editing hold. Write the tests first in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/recordCommit.test.ts, inside describe('held contested paths (MOE_CONTESTED_HELD)'):

(1) A committed landing with skipped [{path:'docs/x.md', code:'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING(task-peer)'}] and contested [{path:'docs/x.md', taskId:'task-peer'}]:
- posts a task-channel line starting `MOE_CONTESTED_HELD task=<id>: docs/x.md(task-peer)`;
- that line contains the editing remedy and neither the untouched nor the strict remedy;
- #governors is alerted once.

(2) Error-handling cases: the codes `MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING(peer)` and `MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING()`, and an editing code on an unnormalisable path such as '../x', are not holds and do not throw. There is no MOE_CONTESTED_HELD line, and no governors alert when nothing else qualifies.

(3) One untouched hold plus one editing hold give a single line naming both paths. Its remedies come in the order untouched, editing, never.

Then implement in packages/moe-daemon/src/tools/recordCommit.ts:
- Add `CONTESTED_EDITING_RE = /^MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING\((task-[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)\)$/` next to CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED_RE.
- Add the constant HELD_REMEDY_EDITING with exactly this text: 'MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING: a contesting peer task was mid-step on the path with an active session at this landing, so this session\'s editing tool did not release it (the file can carry that peer\'s unfinished hunks). Coordinate that peer; after its step completes, either this task\'s own assignee session edits the path with a wrapper-observed successful editing tool before the next landing, or the peer\'s own landing carries these bytes (name its commit in the summary).'
- Change HeldPath.strict:boolean to kind: 'untouched' | 'editing' | 'strict'. Untouched and editing holds take the peer from their code; a strict hold takes it from the contested entry.
- heldContestedLine joins the remedies in the order untouched, editing, strict, then HELD_REMEDY_NEVER.

Error handling stays as it is: tolerantNormalizePath skips bad paths, and a failed chat post never changes the ledger outcome (the existing try/catch). Every existing held-path test stays green unchanged.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Make the peer set count an IN_PROGRESS step's planned affectedFiles. Not needed: collectPeerPaths already unions every step's files, so task-9cc13170 was in the PEER map at 06:22:35. It shared one entry with task-66e8d7d1, which sorts first and so became the named claimant. Neither task waits on task-574c0b36 (checked). (2) Fix only the trailer. Not enough: the sweep happened because 574c0b36's own Edit (a TOOL witness) releases a contested path whatever else is in the file, and 9cc13170 was mid-step-4 on it, so its unfinished hunks landed. This is the broken-HEAD class in mem gotcha-shared-file-hunks-land-under-first-committer. (3) A daemon-only hold via excludePrefixes or a policy override. Rejected: it hides the reason, applies to every path, and the TOOL tier is wrapper-side. (4) Hunk-level staging. Rejected as too risky. Chosen: this task makes the daemon expose taskIds and editingTaskIds and has record_commit recognise MOE_ATTR_CONTESTED_EDITING. task-01f37ac63316409ab581f5a189002cb8 (BACKLOG; depends on this task and on task-a2f243a1, which has the wrapper files dirty) makes moe-agent.{sh,ps1} hold and name the peers.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: getCommitScope visits peers in id order: the first claimant wins taskId and peerActive is ORed. touchedFiles is updated only by record_commit at landing, so mid-step a peer's claim is its IN_PROGRESS step's affectedFiles (planned tier). On the wrapper side, resolve_attribution does PEER.setdefault(taskId), ANDs PEER_IDLE across entries and prints only PEER[pk] in the Moe-Contested trailer. record_commit classifies holds only from skip codes (CONTESTED_UNTOUCHED_RE, the strict code).
